clue.text: Call about female killer, rough work of 1 down

indicators.note: about means one word wraps around the other, here the call goes round the female

parts.note: to call out is to cry
her stands for a female person
an orc is a killer whale, the orca
rough as in harsh means hard

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a murderous woman over some crude piece of Russian writing.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' refers to the Russian dramatist's name in that light, so the definition is one of his plays; 'killer' is the whale, not a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherry Orchard is a celebrated late play by the Russian dramatist named at 1 down.

clue.text: Russian money sent when uttered?

indicators.note: when uttered means the words are said out loud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: money is a cheque, and sent is off, as in sent off by post

explanation.surface: A question about whether Russian cash goes out when somebody speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'cheque off' gives the name of the Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a Russian playwright and short-story writer, so the name stands for a Russian.

clue.text: Emigrant to be corrosive about value of "silver" coin

indicators.note: about means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: acid that is corrosive eats away, so to be corrosive is to eat
the ten-pence coin is silver-coloured, and ten pence is X (Roman ten) plus P for pence

explanation.surface: An emigrant is said to be acidic about what an old silver coin is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes mark that the UK 10p coin only looks silver (it is cupronickel); its value, 10p, is written XP.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is someone who lives outside their native country, an emigrant from it.

clue.text: What (in play) of the Sun, heartlessly roaming after pointy stag?

indicators.note: after means the roaming letters come behind the stag in the answer

parts.note: a royal is a stag with twelve or more points to its antlers

indicators.note: roaming means the remaining letters wander into a new order
heartlessly means the central letters of the words are taken out

explanation.surface: A riddle about what happens in a drama to the sun, wandering cruelly after a stag with antlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes ES from THESUN, and 'roaming' turns THUN into HUNT. Peter Shaffer's play is The Royal Hunt of the Sun, so 'of the Sun' also completes the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title The Royal Hunt of the Sun names what of the Sun a play is about: its royal hunt.

clue.text: See 25
Dispose of complaint, missing drug when inside 1 down's work

indicators.note: when inside means the shortened complaint sits within the word for dispose of

parts.note: to dispose of goods is to sell them

indicators.note: missing means the drug's letter is left out of the complaint

parts.note: an ague is a feverish complaint
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an illness, without drugs, while absorbed in a Russian author's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '1 down's work' points to a play by the Russian writer at 1 down; 'complaint' is an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seagull is one of the best-known plays by the Russian named at 1 down.

clue.text: Sort of fund opening to subsidise drinker

indicators.note: opening to means only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: Some kind of fund is set up to pay for a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is a reserve of money kept for illicit or improper purposes.

clue.text: Set about cleric wrongly put in goal

indicators.note: put in means the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for goal

parts.note: a goal or aim is an end

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of the word are set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is wrongly placed in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns CLERIC into CIRCLE; 'Set about' looks like 'began', but here it means surrounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set about with walls is surrounded by them, ringed on every side.

clue.text: Agent general coming in, ready for bed

indicators.note: coming in means the general enters the middle of the agent

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A general arrives to find an operative who is ready to turn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy is drowsy and so ready to go to bed.

clue.text: Coppers, nearly one pound, in drawer

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: copper coins are pence
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Small change, almost a pound, kept in a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; it is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a tool for drawing, so it is literally a drawer.

clue.text: Hype's terrible, breaking novel — not enough puff with it

indicators.note: breaking means the shuffled letters burst into the middle of the novel

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

indicators.note: terrible means the letters are in a bad state, jumbled

parts.note: here Hype's is short for hype is, so the s counts

explanation.surface: Publicity is awful for a book, leaving it short of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not enough puff with it' describes a lung condition; 'novel' is a noun naming a Jane Austen book, not the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease leaving the sufferer short of breath.

clue.text: Welsh boy enveloped in extraordinary lunacy in 1 down's work

indicators.note: enveloped in means the Welsh name is wrapped inside the jumbled letters
extraordinary means the letters are put out of their ordinary order

parts.note: Evan is a typically Welsh boy's name

explanation.surface: A Welshman is caught up in remarkable madness during a Russian play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' gives UNCLY, the jumble of the madness word; 'Welsh boy' is a first name typical of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Vanya is a major play by the Russian dramatist at 1 down.

clue.text: The Greek, northern English and Spanish pub

parts.note: ho is the Greek word for the
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t', as in down t' pit
el is the Spanish for the, the word carried over from the start of the clue

explanation.surface: A list of drinking places from Greece, the north of England and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' serves all three languages: HO in Greek, T' in Yorkshire speech, EL in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a public house in Australian usage and loosely an inn, a place serving drinks.

clue.text: Lozenge makes Spooner divest himself of whip

indicators.note: makes Spooner means the opening sounds of two words are swapped, as Rev. Spooner did

parts.note: to divest oneself of clothing is to doff it
a crop is a short riding whip

explanation.surface: A sweet for the throat leads a clergyman to put down his riding whip.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds gives COFF DROP, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a medicated sweet sucked to soothe a cough.

clue.text: Are you said to be split into "live" and "computer generated"?

indicators.note: into means the second letter is also placed within the word for live
split means the two letters are separated, each going into the word on its own

parts.note: live as in a live wire, full of life, is vital
said aloud, the letter R sounds like are
said aloud, the letter U sounds like you

explanation.surface: A question on whether text-speak can be divided between real and digital.
explanation.walkthrough: R and U are split, so R goes after VI and U after T: VI-R-T-U-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtual describes something simulated by a computer rather than existing physically.

clue.text: Fellow with float, maybe German and south Italian circulating

indicators.note: circulating means the Italian goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A German and an Italian from the south go about with a floating thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and' gives UND, not 'German' plus a link; a roundsman's float is a British milk delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman delivers goods on a regular round, such as a milkman driving an electric milk float.

clue.text: Grade sign after letters as book of 25 4 across

indicators.note: after means the impresario and sign follow the letters in the answer

parts.note: Litt. abbreviates letters, as in the degree D.Litt, Doctor of Letters
Lew Grade was a British television impresario
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A grade mark comes after some letters, as a book about siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grade' is the surname of Lew Grade, the British TV mogul. Commenters noted the book has four sisters, not three.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about the four March sisters.

clue.text: Wordbook found on the Lizard?

parts.note: taken as written
saurus is the Greek-derived word for lizard, as in dinosaur names

explanation.surface: Asking whether a dictionary was discovered on the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall, but here it is the reptile, Greek sauros.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of words grouped by meaning, a wordbook.

clue.text: Exactly what Kipling wrote

definitions.meaning: Rudyard Kipling wrote the ... Stories for children

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exactly so and is also the title of Kipling's book of animal origin tales.

clue.text: See 1 across
Domain of 15 medicine, if regulated

indicators.note: regulated means the letters are put in an ordered new arrangement

parts.note: 15 is the word little, and little medicine means the word shortened to med

explanation.surface: A domain of small medicines is regulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is LITTLE, so 'little medicine' is MED; 'regulated' rearranges OF+MED+IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiefdom is the territory held under a feudal lord, his domain.

clue.text: Comedian with a record? Not far off

parts.note: having form means having a criminal record
by as in close by means near, not far off

explanation.surface: A comic with a disc to his name, not too far away.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby was an English comedian and ukulele-playing singer; 'record' suggests music but means a police record.
explanation.definitionFit: George Formby was a popular British comedian and entertainer of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: How I think to take care of my teeth?

parts.note: to mind is to look after or take care of
a set is a full set of false teeth

explanation.surface: Someone muses on looking after their dentures.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's habitual way of thinking or mental attitude.

clue.text: Wasted opportunity with almost complete mushroom

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: blewits is the full name of an edible lilac-stemmed mushroom

explanation.surface: A missed chance with a nearly whole fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted opportunity' is a verb phrase: you blew it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone blew it means they wasted their chance.

clue.text: Shepherdess takes boy and clingy girl back on wheels

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: back means the girl's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name and ivy is a clinging plant
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A shepherdess takes a boy and a needy girl home by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IVY into YVI. 'Shepherdess' is a woman who tends a flock, the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman vicar is a pastor, a shepherd of her flock of parishioners.

clue.text: See 10
1 down has footballer topped and tailed

indicators.note: topped and tailed means the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: Eric Cantona was a French footballer at Manchester United

explanation.surface: A Russian writer owns a soccer player who has had his head and feet chopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton was Chekhov's first name.

clue.text: 1 down's work gives very little change to the Maquis

indicators.note: very little change to means only one letter moves, a single place along

parts.note: the Maquis were the French Resistance fighters in WWII, the resisters

explanation.surface: A Russian play barely alters the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the R of THE RESISTERS one place earlier gives THREE SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Three Sisters is a classic play by the Russian dramatist named at 1 down.

clue.text: See 15
Light grey stuff used in perfumery

parts.note: amber is a traffic light colour
gris is French for grey

explanation.surface: A pale grey substance used to make scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light grey' reads as one colour; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales used as a fixative in perfumes.

clue.text: Parliament, centre of dirty dogs, keeping back grass

indicators.note: keeping means the central letters hold the reversed grass inside them
centre of means only the middle letters of the phrase are used
back means the word for grass is read backwards

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: A legislature's core is full of scoundrels holding the grass back.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of DIRTY DOGS are TYD; 'back' makes NWAL from LAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynwald is the parliament of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Yes, when posted

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived
a letter posted is sent

explanation.surface: Yes, at the time of mailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement, the saying of yes.
